eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models and official National Weather Service guidance point to a daily high near 88°F in Miami on September 1, 2026, as scattered to numerous afternoon thunderstorms develop after 1 p.m. and limit further warming.**  

Typical early-September conditions feature high humidity, light easterly flow, and sea-breeze-driven instability that triggers convection by midday, often causing temperatures to peak in the upper 80s before falling into the mid-80s. The NWS explicitly forecasts a high near 88°F with 50% storm chances and heat indices to 104°F, while other guidance ranges from 84–89°F. Historical averages sit near 90°F, but the current pattern of widespread moisture and slow-moving storms favors the lower end of the normal range. This consensus explains why the 88–89°F bin leads market-implied odds at 58%, ahead of 90–91°F at 26.5%. No anomalous heat or suppressed convection is indicated that would shift probabilities higher.

September 1 observations show surface temperatures near 19 °C with high humidity and light southwesterly flow, setting up a mild start to the period. Ensemble guidance and short-range runs indicate the peak will occur in the afternoon, with limited precipitation risk and stable pressure supporting the upper end of the range. Historical September averages for Helsinki (roughly 16–18 °C highs) are being exceeded due to the current synoptic pattern, but no extreme warmth is expected.

The market’s heavy weighting on 20 °C (58.5 %) and 21 °C (36.5 %) reflects this tight forecast cluster, with lower probabilities assigned to outliers as model agreement strengthens ahead of resolution. Minor revisions in the final 12–24 hours could shift outcomes within this narrow band.

eventMetadata.context_description: A cold front tied to an extratropical cyclone has swept through São Paulo on September 1, advecting cooler southerly air and producing widespread cloud cover, showers, and gusty winds that suppress daytime heating. Post-frontal conditions on September 2 feature southeasterly flow, partial clearing, and dew points near 10–12 °C, limiting maximum temperatures. Official guidance from INMET, Climatempo, and global models (GFS/ECMWF) converges on highs of 19–20 °C, with minor spread arising from differences in predicted insolation, boundary-layer mixing, and urban heat-island effects. Trader consensus clustering around 20–21 °C reflects this narrow uncertainty band and the historical tendency for post-frontal days to finish 2–4 °C below September climatology.

**Current forecasts from multiple models (including GFS, ECMWF, and regional guidance) show a strong consensus for a daily high near 29–31°C in Jinan on September 2 under clear to mostly sunny skies, light northeast winds, and stable high pressure.** 

This positions the 26°C-or-higher outcome at 95% implied probability, consistent with the September climatological average high of ~26°C and the absence of any cooling factors such as frontal passages or increased cloud cover. Official monitoring from agencies like the China Meteorological Administration aligns with these projections, with minimal model spread and no signals of significant deviation. 

Realistic challenges to this outcome would require rapid changes in steering patterns or unexpected convective development, though current guidance indicates low probability of such shifts before resolution. Traders are weighting the skin-in-the-game consensus toward the dominant forecast range given the short lead time and high model agreement.

Stable high pressure, light westerly winds, and minimal cloud cover support modest daytime heating without exceeding historical September extremes. Updated model consensus and the absence of anomalous atmospheric patterns in the past 48 hours reinforce trader focus on the narrow 31–33°C band ahead of final observational data.

No significant synoptic changes (such as a cold front or increased moisture) are expected in the next 48 hours, keeping the temperature distribution tightly centered near the observed recent values. Updated model runs and the next official Chongqing Meteorological Bureau briefing will provide the final inputs before market resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Beijing Capital International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 3 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=zbaa

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Current forecasts from official and major meteorological sources (CMA, Yr.no, WeatherBug, and others) indicate a sunny, clear day on September 3 with a high near 31–33 °C under southerly or light variable winds and minimal cloud cover.** This positions 32 °C and 33 °C as the leading market outcomes (combined ~64 % implied probability), consistent with the ongoing late-summer warming trend and absence of precipitation or significant frontal activity.

Beijing’s early-September climatology features an average daily high of ~28.6 °C, but recent model runs show above-average insolation and a building high-pressure ridge that has already lifted daytime maxima from the upper 20s °C earlier in the week. Ensemble guidance shows tight clustering around 31–32 °C, with limited upside risk to 34 °C only if boundary-layer mixing or downslope warming exceeds current expectations; downside to 30 °C or below appears unlikely given the stable synoptic pattern.

Key upcoming data points include the next CMA and ECMWF model cycles plus any updated surface observations on September 2, which could refine the exact peak if afternoon heating deviates from the consensus. Traders are effectively pricing the most probable range under current clear-sky, light-wind conditions while assigning low probability to outliers.
